```plato

    // The inverse affine map, paired with whether one exists. The linear block is
    // inverted by the 2x2 adjugate and the translation row carried back through
    // it. When the determinant is smaller than Number.Epsilon the matrix is
    // singular: the all-NaN matrix and `false` are returned.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertible_matrix
    Invert(self: Matrix3x2): Tuple2<Matrix3x2, Boolean> {
        var m11 = self.Row1.X;
        var m12 = self.Row1.Y;
        var m21 = self.Row2.X;
        var m22 = self.Row2.Y;
        var m31 = self.Row3.X;
        var m32 = self.Row3.Y;
        var det = m11 * m22 - m21 * m12;
        var invDet = 1.0 / det;
        var inverse = Matrix3x2(
            Number2(m22 * invDet, -m12 * invDet),
            Number2(-m21 * invDet, m11 * invDet),
            Number2((m21 * m32 - m31 * m22) * invDet, (m31 * m12 - m11 * m32) * invDet));
        var ok = det.Abs >= Number.Epsilon;
        return (ok ? inverse : Matrix3x2.NotANumber, ok);
    }
```

```plato
    // The inverse map, by the adjugate over the determinant. A singular matrix
    // (see CanInvert) yields the all-NaN matrix, as System.Numerics does rather
    // than signalling.
    Invert(self: Matrix4x4): Matrix4x4
        => self.CanInvert
            ? self.Adjugate * (1.0 / self.Determinant)
            : Matrix4x4.NotANumber;
```
